problem: Prior photo-realistic navigation tasks give the agent little or no way to get help. R2R-style VLN has no help-requesting. VNLA's advisor is always present and speaks templated language. CVDN's human dialog is unavailable once the agent leaves the collected trajectories. So no benchmark lets an agent request natural, multimodal (language + image) help that adapts to where it is while navigating to an object.
motivation: Agents in unknown environments often cannot finish tasks alone. Humans are rich but scarce helpers, so agents must learn to ask mindfully and to interpret the help. Real human help is interpersonal (assistants are scattered in the environment), reactive (it gives partial progress based on local knowledge) and multimodal. The simulator can be built with no extra annotation cost by reusing R2R instructions as 'routes' known to simulated assistants.
key_idea: Build a simulator (HANNA) where an object-finding agent can request help from simulated assistants (ANNA) who reply with an R2R natural-language instruction plus a target-view image as a subtask. Train a hierarchical memory-augmented agent with retrospective, curiosity-encouraging imitation learning: the help-request teacher labels 'lost' using the agent's own future trajectory, and a loss penalizes repeating past wrong actions.
insight: Language-based help is what drives generalization. Removing language and keeping only the target image drops test-unseen SR from 47.45 to 31.88 (−15.17), but only −3.42 on seen environments, where the agent can memorize. The curiosity-encouraging loss cuts looping: navigation-mistake repeat falls 25.00%→17.85% and help-request repeat 40.17%→21.10%, raising test-unseen SR 43.12→47.45. It slightly hurts memorization, though: val-seen SPL is 70.18 without it vs 63.02 with it. The ablation also exposes a tension in joint training. Condition (reason) prediction boosts val-seen SR 72.33→87.24 but slightly lowers val-unseen SR (47.88→45.64). A better navigation policy produces fewer positive 'need help' examples for training the help-request policy.
method: HANNA simulator / ANNA assistants: Matterport3D nav graph; the agent must stop within 2 m of any instance of the requested object ('find X'). Assistants are sets of language-assisted R2R routes (avg 211 routes over 125 locations per environment); help can be requested when a route start is within ε_attn = 2 m. On request, ANNA picks the route and departure node closest to the goal and returns (instruction, departure-view image); on departure it gives the goal-view image.
Route-construction theory: a lemma shows Θ(N log N) instructions (spanning tree plus 2^i-th ancestor paths) suffice to connect any location pair with O(log N) instructions.

Two policies: a navigation policy over the panoramic action space (adjacent viewpoint + camera change, plus stop, which also departs a route) and a help-request policy (request_help / do_nothing). Imitation learning is framed as I3L (Imitation Learning with Indirect Intervention); the nav teacher gives the shortest-path next step to the goal or subtask target.

Retrospective interpretable help-request teacher: labels are computed after the episode ends. Request help if (lost: will never get strictly closer to target, OR uncertain_wrong: nav-distribution efficiency (base-37 entropy) ≥ γ = 0.25 and argmax ≠ teacher) AND never_asked here. A reason classifier is trained with a multi-label binary logistic loss on the 3 conditions.
Curiosity-encouraging loss: adds α·mean log-prob of non-reference actions the agent already took at the same location under the same instruction (α = 1), discouraging repeated mistakes.

Hierarchical memory-augmented Transformer-style architecture: a text encoder re-encodes the instruction whenever the task switches. An inter-task self-attention module is reset on each task switch and uses a local ResNet-style learned time encoding. An intra-task module covers the whole episode and uses a cosine-similarity attention (SimAttend, threshold 0.9) to retrieve past states in near-identical situations, then computes h = h̄ − β·h̃ with a learned sigmoid gate β. Inputs are ResNet-152 36-view panoramic features, a target-similarity vector, and the previous action; the help network also takes the nav action distribution.

setting.backbone: custom hierarchical Transformer-style memory-augmented policy networks (nav + help-request), trained from scratch on frozen ImageNet ResNet-152 features
setting.training_data: HANNA train split: 82,484 object-finding tasks over 51 Matterport3D environments with 8,586 ANNA instructions reused from R2R (289 object types); imitation learning with teacher access to GT states
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36-view ResNet-152 features) of current view, plus target-view panorama features from assistance and the natural-language instruction; no location/GPS
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space, stop) + binary request_help/do_nothing
setting.privileged: none for the agent at test time (assistants use GT goal locations by design of the task); success radius 2 m, 50 eval steps

numbers_note: Two evaluation schemes are reported. The main EMNLP tables use batch size 32 with mini-batch resetting, which is non-deterministic. Appendix tables use batch size 1 (deterministic), and the authors strongly recommend citing those. 'Test SeenEnv' (seen environments, new tasks/instructions) is mapped to split 'test'; 'Test UnseenAll' is mapped to 'test-unseen'. Help-request condition accuracy/precision/recall are given only in a figure.
results: On HANNA test-unseen the agent reaches 47.45% SR / 25.50 SPL (45.43 / 25.02 under the recommended batch-size-1 eval), vs 8.10% for a learned agent without assistance. On test seen-environments it reaches 88.37% SR (86.67 at batch size 1), with 2.9 requests per task. The learned help-request policy beats RandomAsk (37.05) and AskEvery5 (34.42) on test-unseen while making fewer requests. The architecture beats an LSTM encoder-decoder (RCM-style) by +28.2 SR (47.45 vs 19.25). A large gap remains to perfect assistance interpretation (83.56 SR unseen).
limitations: Assistance is simulated from randomly placed R2R routes with GT-optimal route/departure selection. The agent can only signal for help rather than ask natural-language questions, and nothing is evaluated on real robots.
Instruction following is still weak in unseen environments: 45–47% SR vs 79–84% with perfect assistance interpretation. Help-condition prediction recall is below 50%.

Mini-batch resetting made the original results depend on batch composition. Jointly training nav and help-request policies creates a trade-off: better navigation leaves fewer positive examples for learning when to ask.
